proof:
# A common stress on arbitrary diffuse-curvature contact strata

This is a necessary structural theorem for an attained unrestricted local
minimum with finitely many positive planar fibers. It does not assume smooth
curvature, mutually absolutely continuous fiber curvatures, or stable Jensen
contact intervals. Curvature atoms remain outside its almost-everywhere
conclusion. It does not by itself prove the OC numerical bound.

## 1. Finite base, finite cap cover, and notation

Let K_z, z in a finite lattice-convex base P, be positive planar convex
fibers satisfying all Jensen Minkowski containments. Assume their maximum
mixed halfspace depth beta>0 is locally minimal under sufficiently small
compatible fiber deformations. Put M=sum_z area(K_z) and D=beta M.

Fix one critical whole-fiber cap circuit at each deepest index, with all its
caps of absolute mass D and nonzero continuous normals. Fix slack circuits
at the remaining indices. The circuits provide an exact finite CLOSED cover
of every fiber. Their existence and the interior-anchor/cap-normal facts
are as in critical-cap-cover-and-volume-variation.md. Let H_1,...,H_N be
the selected critical caps.

For each z write h_z(theta) for its support function, and

    R_z=h_z+h_z''                 (curvature measure),
    R=sum_z R_z^c,   r_z=dR_z^c/dR,

where the superscript c means the nonatomic part. Thus r_z>=0 and sum r_z=1
R-almost everywhere.

There are finitely many necessary Jensen support inequalities

    g_a(theta)=sum_z q_az h_z(theta)>=0,       a=1,...,A.

Indeed for each target index the barycentric representation set is a compact
finite-dimensional polytope; it suffices to use its finitely many extreme
representations. Their coefficients are fixed and independent of theta.
At any angle let A(theta)={a:g_a(theta)=0}, J(theta)={z:r_z(theta)>0}, and

    L(theta)={v:q_a.v=0 for a in A(theta),
                    v_z=0 for z outside J(theta)}.          (1)

## 2. Two elementary diffuse-curvature facts

First, for a fixed cap line in a positive planar fiber, the normal angles
whose exposed face meets that line have zero nonatomic curvature measure.
If the line cuts the interior, its intersection with the boundary consists
of at most two points. The normal cone of a boundary point has curvature
zero on its interior, since there h(theta)=x.n(theta) is homogeneous; its
endpoints can carry only curvature atoms. If the line supports a boundary
segment, add the one facet normal, also an atom. The remaining endpoint
normal cones have the same property. A disjoint line gives no such angles.

Outside this negligible set, the ENTIRE exposed face is strictly in or
strictly outside the cap. The same strict sign holds on a neighborhood of
the angle, with a positive margin: the exposed-face map is upper
semicontinuous, as follows by taking limits of support-maximizing points.

Consequently, for R-almost every theta and every z in J(theta), all N cap
memberships are strictly defined. At EVERY angle whose entire exposed face
has a strict sign, including facet-atom angles, put I_jz(theta)=1 for a
face strictly inside H_j and 0 for one strictly outside. Assign arbitrary
values only where the exposed face meets the cap line. These bad angles
do not affect r_z dR; moreover every acceleration used below vanishes on a
neighborhood of the bad faces in each fiber it changes. Thus the full-R_z
first-mass integrals in (5), including their atoms, are unambiguous.

Second, on the zero set of a Jensen gap one has

    sum_z q_az r_z(theta)=0       R-almost everywhere on {g_a=0}. (2)

To prove this, g_a is Lipschitz and g_a' is BV, because support functions
have finite distributional second derivatives. At each zero where it is
differentiable, nonnegativity gives g_a'=0. Derivative jumps are countable.
BV locality gives (D^c g_a')|_{g_a=0}=0, and g_a dtheta also vanishes there.
Thus the nonatomic part of g_a''+g_a=sum_z q_az R_z vanishes on the zero
set, proving (2). The locality proof with the truncations
epsilon arctan(t/epsilon), including its jump terms, is given in
curvature-potential-locality-on-singular-support.md.

Equations (1),(2) imply

    r(theta) belongs to L(theta)                 R-almost everywhere. (3)

## 3. Guarded source families exist on arbitrary contact sets

Stratify R by the FINITELY many patterns consisting of:

* the exact set A0 of zero Jensen gaps;
* the exact positive curvature-coordinate set J0;
* the strict cap-membership values I_jz for z in J0.

Discard the null sets from Section2. For every point in a remaining stratum,
all inactive gaps are positive and the cap memberships on J0 persist on
some open interval. Choose rational guard intervals with compact closure
inside these strict neighborhoods and of length less than pi. They give a
countable cover. Restrict further to levels min_(z in J0)r_z>=1/k and to
compact subintervals inside the guards. Define each resulting source by

    nu=(1/k) R restricted to that stratum, level, and compact interval.

Ignore zero sources. Each source is nonatomic, is dominated by R_z for
every z in J0, and is supported on {g_a=0:a in A0}. These countably many
sources exhaust the diffuse curvature up to an R-null set.

Put L_A0,J0=ker{q_a:a in A0} intersect {v outside J0=0}. For v in this
space, the compact Green-potential variation delta h_z=v_z phi is genuinely
feasible. Its curvature perturbations are dominated by the source fiber
curvatures. More importantly,

    delta g_a=(q_a.v)phi=0 identically for a in A0,

even at nearby angles where that original gap is not zero. Every other gap
has a uniform positive margin on the compact guard. Thus no stability of
the original contact set is needed. The affected cap memberships are fixed
on the guard, and the other fiber coordinates do not move.

The two sine/cosine endpoint moments make phi compactly supported. Impose
also integral phi dR_z=0 for all fibers. The finite-dimensional construction
in candidate ed7be0e1efdfe13b gives a nonzero such phi with
Q(phi)=integral(phi^2-phi'^2)<0. Rescaling gives the second mass generator

    B0(v)=-sum_z v_z^2,
    Bj(v)=-sum_z I_jz v_z^2.                                (4)

All its first objective and cap masses are zero.

## 4. One global separation, not a separate stress on each stratum

Every finite conic combination of ALL generators (4) is realizable at once.
For a finite list of sources choose distinct points in their supports and
disjoint small intervals inside their respective guards. Nonatomic positive
sources permit these choices even if the source measures overlap. Construct
and normalize each orthogonal Green potential separately. Cross area terms
vanish by disjoint supports.

For acceleration tests omit the zero-mass orthogonality conditions. Allow
finite linear combinations from all source families. Each is a signed
feasible variation: curvature domination constants add finitely, and each
nonzero change of any Jensen gap is confined to finitely many regions on
which that gap is uniformly positive.

As cap memberships now vary between guards, use the FULL finite first-mass
feature vector

    T0(delta h)=sum_z integral delta h_z dR_z,
    Tj(delta h)=sum_z integral I_jz(theta)delta h_z(theta)dR_z(theta),
                           j=1,...,N.                      (5)

This replaces the per-fiber features used on a single fixed-membership arc.
Its image is a subspace of R^(N+1), so finitely many actual acceleration
tests span it. No infinite-dimensional parameter compactness is assumed.

Adjoin the signed joint continuous homotheties and the finite cap parameter
motions satisfying the exact linear cover constraints. The robust cap
gradient sets retain one consistent measurable trace at each coincidence.
The direct-budget epigraph separation of
candidate f27caa3ee43c68e2 applies to the cone generated by all
(4), using the finite feature model (5). Its proof requires neither a
closed image cone nor differentiable cap quantiles.

It gives ONE collection lambda_j>=0, common to every stratum, with

    sum_j lambda_j=1/beta.                                  (6)

The normalization follows from the two exact joint homotheties, on which
the objective derivatives are +/-2M and EVERY allowed cap gradient is
+/-2D. The same separator gives, for every occurring guarded source pattern,

    sum_z W_z v_z^2>=0       for every v in L_A0,J0,
    W_z=1-sum_j lambda_j I_jz.                              (7)

## 5. Almost-everywhere nullspace conclusion

Fix a source, its pattern, and v in L_A0,J0. On its guard the relevant I_jz
are constant for z in J0; the other v coordinates vanish. First-order
annihilation for EVERY Green-potential acceleration from this source says

    integral phi dmu_v=0,       mu_v=sum_z W_z v_z R_z.

The singular-support potential-locality lemma gives

    (mu_v)^c restricted to supp(nu)=0.

Take a finite basis of L_A0,J0, then the countable union over guarded level
sources. Along with (3), this proves that for R-almost every theta,

    r(theta) in L(theta),
    diag(W(theta)) r(theta) orthogonal to L(theta),
    sum_z W_z(theta) v_z^2>=0 for every v in L(theta),        (8)

where W_z(theta)=1-sum_j lambda_j I_jz(theta). In particular the actual
curvature-density vector lies in the nullspace of the positive-semidefinite
diagonal form restricted to its exact active-contact/source subspace.

The multiplier lambda is the SAME in (6)--(8) at almost every normal. No
independent convenient stress was chosen for different contact strata.
This theorem controls diffuse curvature even on singular or Cantor contact
sets. It does not classify curvature atoms or turn (8) into the missing
global numerical cap bound without an additional argument.
